flow.costPlain: Making and shipping the clothes — this quarter it is reduced by $134.5M of tariff refunds, which is why gross margin looks unusually strong.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, marketing and head-office costs — including $13.4M of proxy-contest costs this quarter.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of acquired intangible assets.

follow100Note: By channel: stores brought in $48.58 of every $100, e-commerce $38.68 and other channels $12.72. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The release gives only percentage changes by region; the dollar splits are from Lululemon's Q2 fiscal 2026 Form 10-Q. Lululemon calls this fiscal year '2026' — it ends January 31, 2027.
oneTimers: Lululemon received $134.5M of IEEPA tariff refunds in the quarter, booked as a reduction of cost of goods sold — worth about 560 basis points of gross margin and, with $4.1M of related interest, $0.86 of EPS. Without the refunds, gross margin would have fallen.
Proxy-contest costs of $13.4M sit inside SG&A ($24.8M across the first two quarters).
Guidance was cut with this release: fiscal 2026 revenue is now expected at $10.350–10.500B (down 5–7%) and EPS at $9.48–$9.73, assuming no further tariff refunds.
otherDetail: Other income of $13.7M includes $4.1M of interest linked to the tariff refunds.
pngFooterNote: Region dollar splits are from Lululemon's Form 10-Q.

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: The engine market stalled: revenue fell 8% and comparable sales fell 12% (U.S. revenue −8%, Canada −11%). Two of every three dollars still come from here, which is why the whole company shrank.

segments.name: China Mainland
segments.note: Revenue rose 4% as reported, though in constant currency it fell 2% and comparable sales fell 2% — growth has cooled from the boom years.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.note: Europe, Asia-Pacific outside China and elsewhere: revenue up 5% as reported, comparable sales down 4%.

takeaways.text: Americas comparable sales fell 12% and regional revenue fell 8% to $1,617M. China grew just 4% as reported (−2% in constant currency). Total comparable sales fell 9% — this is a demand problem, not a supply one.
takeaways.title: The home market is shrinking fast

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 200 basis points to 60.5% only because tariff refunds added roughly 560 points. Underneath, product margins fell on higher tariffs and heavier markdowns — the refund made a weak quarter look respectable.
takeaways.title: A tariff refund dressed up the margin

takeaways.text: Management cut the full-year outlook to revenue of $10.35–10.50B and EPS of $9.48–9.73, and guided the next quarter down 10–11%. A new CEO, Heidi O'Neill, started the week after this report — she inherits a turnaround.
takeaways.title: The full-year outlook was cut

verdict: Lululemon's revenue fell 4% to $2.4B as the Americas slumped — comparable sales down 12% there — and only a $134.5M tariff refund kept profit looking respectable; management cut the full-year outlook.
